newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to name Pena as energy secretary.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to name Pena as energy secretary.

text.p: President Bill Clinton planned Friday to name his transportation secretary, Federico Pena, as the energy secretary for his second term, White House officials said.
In a last-minute decision, Clinton chose Pena over Elizabeth Moler, chair of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, in order to add a Hispanic to his Cabinet lineup, the officials said.

"Let's put it this way," said one official. "If there had not been another appointment for Hispanics, it would have been noticed. The fact is Hispanics came out in very high numbers for the president in the election."

At an 11:30 a.m. EST (1630 GMT) ceremony, Clinton also was expected to name White House aide Alexis Herman to succeed Robert Reich as labour secretary, after coming under pressure from black groups to appoint more African Americans to his Cabinet, said the officials, who asked not to be identified.

Ending a fiercely fought contest, Clinton chose Herman over Representative Esteban Torres, D-Calif. Hispanic groups had rallied for Torres, while powerful blacks such as civil rights leader Jesse Jackson had pushed Herman. Union groups had fought for former Sen. Harris Wofford, D-Pa.

In addition, Clinton plans to nominate Federal Highway Administration chief Rodney Slater to replace Pena at transportation, and an assistant secretary of Housing and Urban Development, Andrew Cuomo, to replace Henry Cisneros as HUD secretary. Cuomo is the eldest son of former New York Gov. Mario Cuomo.
